From b02da26a992db0c0e2559acbda0fc48d4a2fd337 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Joseph Qi <joseph.qi@linux.alibaba.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Mar 2026 11:22:11 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] ocfs2: fix possible deadlock between unlink and
 dio_end_io_write

ocfs2_unlink takes orphan dir inode_lock first and then ip_alloc_sem,
while in ocfs2_dio_end_io_write, it acquires these locks in reverse order.
This creates an ABBA lock ordering violation on lock classes
ocfs2_sysfile_lock_key[ORPHAN_DIR_SYSTEM_INODE] and
ocfs2_file_ip_alloc_sem_key.

Lock Chain #0 (orphan dir inode_lock -> ip_alloc_sem):
ocfs2_unlink
  ocfs2_prepare_orphan_dir
    ocfs2_lookup_lock_orphan_dir
      inode_lock(orphan_dir_inode) <- lock A
    __ocfs2_prepare_orphan_dir
      ocfs2_prepare_dir_for_insert
        ocfs2_extend_dir
	  ocfs2_expand_inline_dir
	    down_write(&oi->ip_alloc_sem) <- Lock B

Lock Chain #1 (ip_alloc_sem -> orphan dir inode_lock):
ocfs2_dio_end_io_write
  down_write(&oi->ip_alloc_sem) <- Lock B
  ocfs2_del_inode_from_orphan()
    inode_lock(orphan_dir_inode) <- Lock A

Deadlock Scenario:
  CPU0 (unlink)                     CPU1 (dio_end_io_write)
  
diff --git a/fs/ocfs2/aops.c b/fs/ocfs2/aops.c
index 17ba79f443ee..09146b43d1f0 100644
--- a/fs/ocfs2/aops.c
+++ b/fs/ocfs2/aops.c
@@ -2294,8 +2294,6 @@ static int ocfs2_dio_end_io_write(struct inode *inode,
 		goto out;
 	}
 
-	down_write(&oi->ip_alloc_sem);
-
 	/* Delete orphan before acquire i_rwsem. */
 	if (dwc->dw_orphaned) {
 		BUG_ON(dwc->dw_writer_pid != task_pid_nr(current));
@@ -2308,6 +2306,7 @@ static int ocfs2_dio_end_io_write(struct inode *inode,
 			mlog_errno(ret);
 	}
 
+	down_write(&oi->ip_alloc_sem);
 	di = (struct ocfs2_dinode *)di_bh->b_data;
 
 	ocfs2_init_dinode_extent_tree(&et, INODE_CACHE(inode), di_bh);
-- 
2.34.1

The patch modifies a single file (`fs/ocfs2/aops.c`) to fix a deadlock between `ocfs2_unlink` and `ocfs2_dio_end_io_write`. The change reorders the acquisition of two locks in `ocfs2_dio_end_io_write`: the `ip_alloc_sem` (lock B) is now taken **after** the orphan directory `inode_lock` (lock A) via `ocfs2_del_inode_from_orphan()`. Previously, `ip_alloc_sem` was acquired first, creating an ABBA pattern with the reverse order in `ocfs2_unlink` (`inode_lock` → `ip_alloc_sem`). By aligning the lock order to match that of `ocfs2_unlink`, the patch eliminates the circular wait condition and prevents the deadlock.
